requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, including paginated results

guide.summary: The supplied GitLab snapshots document OAuth 2.0 app registration and authorization for third-party clients. For listing project issues, the documented read_api scope is the narrowest supplied grant covering the Issues API. read_user and read_repository do not cover it. read_api is broad: it grants read access to the API including all groups and projects, so it is bounded by the connected person's own project access rather than one project. Keyset and offset pagination are documented for the project issues endpoint. Setup, customer approval, and provider review timing are not established by these sources.

findings.title: Register an OAuth application and complete the authorization code flow for the connected person
findings.detail: GitLab documents registering an application via user settings, then sending users to the /oauth/authorize page with the requested scopes so the user approves access. The authorization code is exchanged for an access token. These are setup requirements, not resource actions.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts connect via OAuth as requested.

findings.title: Request the read_api scope for read-only project issue listing
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. The documented project issues endpoint (GET /projects/:id/issues) lists issues for a specified project. The scope's boundary is the connected person's own access: it is not limited to one project and does not restrict to issues only. Read-only use is the app's responsibility because the token itself is not read-only.

steps.title: Register the OAuth application for the connected customer
steps.detail: Developer registers an OAuth application via the user settings applications page, enters a Name and Redirect URI, selects the read_api scope, and saves to obtain the Application ID (client ID) and secret. This prepares code only and does not execute consent or token exchange.
steps.doneWhen: The application exists with a client ID and secret stored outside source code, and its redirect URI and read_api scope are recorded. Registration is not claimed as done until performed.

evidence.quote: registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.
Select Save application . GitLab provides:

fields: Application name and redirect URI: developer-chosen values
Client ID and secret: provided by GitLab after registration

steps.title: Obtain consent and exchange the code for an access token with read_api
steps.detail: The connected customer opens the authorization URL built from the registered client ID, redirect URI, state, PKCE code challenge, and scope=read_api, approves access, and the app exchanges the returned code at the token endpoint. Only the authorized person can approve; the developer must not approve for them.
steps.doneWhen: The customer has approved the request and the app holds an access token with read_api scope. Consent is not claimed as obtained until the customer approves.

steps.title: Read the first page of project issues and record any cursor value
steps.detail: Read only: send GET /api/v4/projects/:id/issues for a representative project the connected person can access, using an OAuth Bearer token in the Authorization header. The endpoint lists all issues for the specified project and returns 20 results by default. Use the project ID supplied by the user. Record any cursor value the response provides; the supplied passages do not document where that value appears in the response. Boundary check: this is a GET-only read within the connected person's own project access. If a read is denied, inspect the token grant and the outgoing request log rather than assuming a narrower or broader permission.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a JSON array of issues for the representative project. Any cursor value supplied by the response is recorded for the continuation step, and no create, update or delete request has been sent.

evidence.quote: Lists all issues for a specified project.
Responses in this API are paginated and return 20 results by default.
--header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
PROJECT_ID: user-provided representative project ID
OAUTH_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the authorization step

steps.title: Request a further page using the cursor parameter
steps.detail: Repeat the same read-only GET request on the same project path and add the cursor query parameter with the value from the previous response. The endpoint documents the cursor parameter for keyset pagination when requesting consecutive pages. The supplied passages do not show how the next cursor value is returned, and they do not document an end condition, so this step does not establish a complete listing. Do not treat an empty page as the end and do not reconstruct URLs. Boundary check: this is a GET-only read within the same access boundary; if a read is denied, inspect the actual token grant and request log.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a further page of issues with the cursor parameter applied. The listing is not reported as complete until a documented end condition is supplied from a source.

steps.title: Confirm a project the connected person cannot access is not readable
steps.detail: Performs one read against a user-provided project the connected person cannot access to confirm the read_api token does not reveal it. A request to a project without access returns 404. This is a nonmutating read and does not prove read-only enforcement by the grant.
steps.doneWhen: The request returns 404 for the excluded project and no issue data is returned. The grant is not claimed to enforce read-only behavior.
